57: Attorney fees under the exceptional-case standard for NOV's refusal to produce the ACA and maintaining the suit after lacking standing; the court found no abuse of discretion.

106: Award of costs to DeLorme; affirmed.
145: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285 denied to Corporate Defendants; court found no abuse of discretion.

146: Exceptional-case finding under 35 U.S.C. § 285 affirmed; district court's exceptionality determination upheld

164: Attorney’s fees under the Lanham Act awarded to Amazon as prevailing party; award affirmed

Because we find that the district court did not err in dismissing Milo & Gabby’s palming off claim and Milo & Gabby made no separate argument regarding the fee award, we affirm the district court’s award of attorney’s fees.
256: Entitlement to attorney's fees under 5 U.S.C. § 1221(g) for the whistleblower prevailing party's prior counsel (Slavet); Board's denial of all fees for that representation reversed and remanded for a reasonable award.
we conclude that Ms. Rumsey carried her burden of showing entitlement to some award of attorney's fees.
280: Exceptional-case finding under 35 U.S.C. § 285 supporting an award of attorney fees to the accused infringer; court affirmed the exceptionality finding.

383: Award of attorney fees to class counsel under the common fund doctrine in lieu of URA statutory fees; the court held the URA preempts common fund recovery and vacated the award.

389: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: the district court held the case was not exceptional as to Astec, so no fees were awarded.
the district court was correct to determine that Astec did not engage in willful infringement and that the case is not exceptional as to Astec.
396: Costs under Federal Circuit Rule 30: DataTreasury's motion to have the Director reimburse printing costs for unnecessary Joint Appendix pages was denied.
We deny the motion, but we caution the Director to carefully evaluate which material it elects to cite in the Joint Appendix
434: Costs awarded to the United States against appellants as a deterrent to frivolous and vexatious litigation
we award costs to the United States.
513: Attorney fee award to Orbis against Buckhorn based on the PLA reversed because Orbis had no contractual basis to recover fees.
the district court's award of fees against Buckhorn is reversed.
514: Whether the district court could award fees against Buckhorn under its inherent power to sanction bad-faith conduct; held no, because the court did not invoke inherent power and no bad faith was shown.

524: EAJA fee request was premature because there has been no final judgment in the appeal; pro se litigants cannot recover EAJA fees after finality.

590: Reimbursement of $3,031.25 in expenses under Fed. R. Civ. P. 37(a)(5)(A) for the motion to compel Gravelle's deposition; the court found the nonattendance was not substantially justified.

591: Attorneys' fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285, 15 U.S.C. § 1117(a) and N.C. Gen. Stat. § 6-21.5: the fee award was vacated because the stated bases could not be reviewed and the case was remanded for reconsideration.

635: Award of attorney fees to Dow under 35 U.S.C. § 285 as an exceptional case; the court affirmed the fee award.
Because the district court did not abuse its discretion in finding the case exceptional and awarding fees, we affirm.
681: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: the district court's denial of defendants' fees motions was vacated and remanded for reconsideration in light of Octane Fitness and Highmark.

685: EAJA attorney fees: IDEA not a prevailing party because it obtained no injunction or money damages, so fees were properly denied
Because IDEA is not a prevailing party, we conclude that the CFC properly denied recovery of attorney's fees under 28 U.S.C. § 2412(b).
704: EAJA attorney fee award: the CIT's determination that the Government's position was not substantially justified, so ICP receives fees under 28 U.S.C. 2412(d)(1)(A); the Government challenged the award on five grounds.
We review the CIT's determinations on whether the Government's position was "substantially justified" for abuse of discretion, see Chiu, 948 F.2d at 713, and the CIT did not abuse its discretion.
751: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: the district court's denial of Newegg's motion for fees as an exceptional case was reversed, so fees are warranted and the case is remanded for calculation of fees.
we hold that the district court abused its discretion in denying Newegg's motion for fees.
803: Denial of Newegg's motion for attorneys' fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285 (exceptional case determination), reviewed for abuse of discretion.

Because we conclude that the district court did not abuse its discretion in finding that SFA's litigating position and the manner in which it litigated this case did not stand out, we affirm the district court's determination that Newegg failed to establish that this case is exceptional under § 285.
835: Denial of attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285 after the inventorship suit ended in summary judgment for the defendants; the court held the case was not exceptional and affirmed the denial.
The district court did not abuse its discretion. We therefore affirm.
1119: Exceptional-case finding and attorneys' fee award under 35 U.S.C. § 285; vacated and remanded because it rested on the reversed willfulness finding

As the court reversed the district court's determination of willful infringement, and the district court's award of attorneys' fees was based on that determination, we vacate the district court's grant of attorneys' fees.
1204: Affirmance of the district court's award of attorney's fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285 to Avid (about $3.94 million).
AIA appeals the award of attorney's fees, but not the amount awarded.
1273: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. §285: district court denied prevailing defendant's fee motion based partly on alleged litigation misconduct; Federal Circuit reversed and remanded for reconsideration under the totality of the circumstances (Octane).
We reverse the district court's denial of attorney's fees, and remand for reconsideration on the totality of the circumstances under Octane.
1438: Vaccine Act attorneys' fees: whether counsel could rely on an impending statute of limitations to establish a reasonable basis for the claim, so that fees were properly denied (Claims Court reversed the special master's fee award).

We conclude that counsel may not use this impending statute of limitations deadline to establish a reasonable basis for Mr. Simmons's claim. Because the special master only found that there was a reasonable basis for Mr. Simmons's claim because of the impending statute of limitations deadline, we conclude that she abused her discretion by misapplying the law. Accordingly, we affirm the Claims Court's decision.
1552: Exceptional case finding under § 285 denied because Promega was not a prevailing party.
Promega cannot be the 'prevailing party' in this litigation under 35 U.S.C. § 285, and we therefore affirm the district court's denial of Promega's motion for an exceptional case finding.
1617: Attorney fees: denial of Vapor Point's motion for exceptional case status and fees not an abuse of discretion.
we do not find that the denial of Vapor Point's motion was an abuse of the district court's discretion.
1673: Whether 35 U.S.C. § 145's 'all the expenses of the proceedings' provision authorizes an award of the USPTO's attorneys' fees to the Director against the applicant, reversing the district court's denial of those fees under the American Rule.
we conclude that the term "expenses" includes the USPTO's attorneys' fees under § 145.
1711: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: the district court's denial of fees on remand under the Octane Fitness standard was affirmed, and reinstatement of the original fee award was rejected.

We see no basis for reinstating the original district court decision, particularly given the district court's determination not to award fees under the new Octane standard and the standard of deferential review under Highmark.
1712: District court award of attorneys' fees as sanctions for Walker's vexatious litigation after the parties settled all claims; fee award affirmed.
The district court correctly concluded that there remained no legitimate reason to continue litigation once the parties entered into a comprehensive settlement of all claims.
1716: Federal Rule of Appellate Procedure 38 sanctions: appeal held frivolous as filed and as argued; damages and double costs awarded to HSN.
we exercise our discretion to impose sanctions in the full amount of HSN's request.
1752: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: denial affirmed because Sealant and AMI are no longer prevailing parties.
The district court's denial of Sealant's attorney fees request, predicated on the now vacated judgment, is therefore affirmed.
1779: Costs awarded to Hulu on appeal in Appeal No. 16-2437.
Costs to Hulu in Appeal No. 16-2437.
1824: Denial of attorney fees and expert fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285 vacated and remanded for reconsideration in light of Octane Fitness.
we vacate the district court's denial of attorney fees and remand for reconsideration in light of Octane Fitness.
1913: Attorneys' fees award and exceptional-case finding under 35 U.S.C. 285 vacated and remanded
we also remand this issue for further consideration by the district court
2032: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: the district court's award of fees for an exceptional case was reversed, so fees were denied or vacated.

We conclude that the district court erred, and thus abused its discretion, in its assessment of "exceptional case," for the record shows that the charge of infringement was reasonable and the litigation was not brought in bad faith or with abusive tactics.
2047: Costs award: the district court's costs judgment was vacated and remanded in light of the court's holding in the companion appeal (No. 14-1406) vacating the merits judgment.

In light of our holding in Shukh v. Seagate Technology, LLC, Case No. 14-1406, vacating and remanding in part the district court's judgment on the merits against Alexander Shukh, we vacate and remand the district court's costs judgment.
2055: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. §285: the district court's award of post-Alice fees to BBB, including fees for the §101 appeal, was upheld.
The district court did not abuse its discretion in awarding BBB its appellate attorney fees.
2122: Attorney fee award under 35 U.S.C. § 285: the district court's exceptional-case finding and award of all requested fees and costs were vacated because several relied-upon circumstances were clearly erroneous or given undue weight.

Because the district court abused its discretion in finding this case exceptional on the grounds articulated for the finding, and because the court's fee calculations were not explained sufficiently, we vacate the district court's award of fees under § 285 and remand for further proceedings consistent with this opinion.
2131: Attorney fees: exceptional-case award upheld under the Lanham Act (trade dress) but vacated to the extent awarded under the Patent Act (§285) or Copyright Act (§505), with remand for clarification.
On the record here, we agree that an award of attorney fees is appropriate, but only with respect to fees awarded under the Lanham Act.
2147: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285, which relied in part on the willfulness finding; award vacated for reconsideration.
It also follows that the district court's award of attorney's fees, which relied in part on the determination of willfulness, must be vacated.
2181: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: denial of exceptional-case fees affirmed; the district court did not abuse its discretion because the vitiation argument was never properly presented at summary judgment.
Therefore, we find that the district court did not abuse its discretion in denying attorneys' fees under § 285.
2192: Request for EAJA litigation costs and attorney fees denied because Colbert was not a prevailing party, and request for appointed counsel denied.
such costs are unavailable because he was not the "prevailing party" at the trial court level and has not prevailed on his appeal.
2307: Attorneys' fees award under 35 U.S.C. § 285, Rule 54(d) and inherent power vacated as premature because the underlying merits decision was reversed in part and vacated in part in the companion appeal.
Because we are reversingin-part and vacating-in-part the underlying merits decision in the Substantive Appeal, we vacate the district court's decision awarding attorneys' fees as premature.
2400: Attorney fees and costs: whether Newegg is a prevailing party entitled to fees and costs under 35 U.S.C. § 285 and Fed. R. Civ. P. 54(d)(1) after Pragmatus's dismissal with prejudice paired with a covenant not to sue; the district court's denial was reversed and remanded.
Accordingly, we hold that the court's analysis in Highway Equipment controls this case, and that Newegg must be regarded as the prevailing party in the underlying litigation.
2439: Denial of attorney and expert fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285, 28 U.S.C. § 1927, and the court's inherent power; the court vacated and remanded for reconsideration after finding no basis for the denial and noting the lowered Octane Fitness standard.
we vacate and remand for the district court to consider whether and the extent to which fees are warranted.
2501: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285. The court vacated the exceptional-case fee award because LBC is no longer the prevailing party after the summary judgment reversal, and did not reach whether the case was exceptional.

2554: Taxation of costs under 28 U.S.C. 1920 for document copying: the district court upheld the taxation of copying costs for documents necessarily obtained for use in the case, whether or not introduced at trial.
We discern no abuse of discretion in the taxation of costs of copying documents found to be 'necessarily obtained for use in the case,' whether or not the documents were introduced into evidence.
2555: Taxation of e-discovery costs: the court held that costs of complying with the parties' ESI agreement are taxable under 1920 as a matter of law, and the district court did not abuse its discretion in taxing them.
We conclude that the district acted within its discretion.
2556: Taxation of trial exemplification costs (trial technology specialists and demonstrative exhibits) under 1920 was within the district court's discretion.
we conclude that the Eighth Circuit would reasonably find the district court's taxation to be within its discretion and within the statute's constraints.
2625: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: the district court denied ADS's request for fees after finding the case not exceptional; the Federal Circuit reversed the exceptional-case determination and remanded for fee calculation.
2715: Attorney fees awarded under 35 U.S.C. § 285 and Rule 37 following the default judgment; vacated along with the judgment.
The awards of damages and attorney fees which resulted from the entry of judgment against Parrot also are vacated.
2766: Rule 11 sanctions imposed as attorneys' fees and costs from the date the invoices were introduced, affirmed.
The district court likewise did not abuse its discretion in granting Rule 11 sanctions.
2832: Costs awarded to the appellant on appeal.
VACATED AND REMANDED Costs to Contreras.
2884: Attorney's fee award on MSPB motion: Board's reduction of four hours for July 22 and August 9, 2014 filings held unsupported by substantial evidence because no fees were requested for those filings.
the reduction of four hours for the filings Mr. Howard made on July 22, 2014 and August 9, 2014 is not supported by substantial evidence.
2886: Attorney's fee award: Board's downward lodestar adjustment for limited results obtained was contrary to Supreme Court and Bywaters precedent because no rare and exceptional case was explained.
a downward reduction to the lodestar should only occur in rare and exceptional cases
2891: Attorney's fees under § 285: denial of accused infringer's supplemental motion for fees as an exceptional case was affirmed.
We conclude that the district court did not abuse its discretion.

3103: Attorneys' fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: district court denied defendants' motion for fees on finding the case not exceptional.
Considering the degree of deference we give to district courts on this matter, we cannot say that the district court abused its discretion by not deeming the case exceptional.
3212: EAJA attorney's fees: whether the claimant was a prevailing party entitled to fees under 28 U.S.C. § 2412(d) after the Veterans Court remand; court reversed the denial of fees.

3254: Attorney fee award under § 285 vacated and remanded for reconsideration
we conclude, Halo warrants a vacatur of those rulings and a remand for reconsideration.
3308: Request for attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285 by Brazabra, declined by the court.
We decline to award fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285 as requested by Brazabra.
3311: Attorney fee award under 42 U.S.C. § 4654(c): court affirmed the reduced lodestar award, including the 30% reduction for work on unsuccessful plaintiffs and the hour reductions.
This reduction, based on the degree of success obtained, was within the Court of Federal Claims' discretion.
3312: Choice of the Adjusted Laffey Matrix over the Kavanaugh Matrix for the hourly rate in the lodestar calculation: no abuse of discretion found.

3313: Application of historical rates rather than rates in effect at the end of litigation under the no-interest rule: upheld.
Therefore, the Court of Federal Claims did not err when it applied historical rates under the no-interest rule.
3347: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: the district court's denial of Vivid Seats' fee request was affirmed because the case was not exceptional.
We affirm the denial of Vivid Seats' motion for attorney's fees.
3395: Lanham Act attorney fees under 15 U.S.C. § 1117(a): court held Octane standard applies to Lanham Act and vacated the denial of fees for remand

3396: Patent Act attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: court vacated the fee award to Romag based on erroneous findings about withdrawal of defenses, indefiniteness, and litigation conduct

3397: Inherent-power award of expert witness fees to Romag, set aside because the underlying finding on indefiniteness was set aside

3587: Sanctions for frivolous appeal under Rule 38 warned against future filings; no fee award made.
Any future such frivolous appeals from Mr. Harris may result in sanctions.
3739: Denial of Indigo's motion for attorney fees under the Texas Theft Liability Act (prevailing-party status after Raytheon's dismissal of its TTLA claim without prejudice)
We disagree that Indigo is entitled to attorney fees for its defense of the TTLA claim and affirm the district court's order denying such fees.
3760: Attorney fee award of the district court, vacated because the district court lacked subject matter jurisdiction.
we vacate the district court’s judgment awarding attorneys’ fees.
3781: Union's arguments that the arbitrator was required to award fees under the Allen factors and that the arbitrator could consider only facts in the merits opinion were rejected; court found the record did not compel a fee award and that the arbitrator could consider facts beyond the merits opinion.

3966: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: court affirmed the district court's finding that the case was exceptional based on the transfer opposition, objectively unreasonable reexamination arguments, and use of a privileged email.

3967: Amount of the § 285 fee award: court approved a full fee award for the entire litigation, including reexamination-related and Texas and California fees, and modified the total to $737,012.34 to correct a double-counted cost.

3977: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: fee award vacated and remanded for reconsideration.

Accordingly, we vacate the district court's injunction and its awards of enhanced damages and attorney fees, and remand to the district court for reconsideration of enhanced damages and attorney fees with respect to only the '966 patent.
4090: Whether guardianship-maintenance expenses are reasonable attorneys' fees or other costs awardable under 42 U.S.C. § 300aa-15(e)(1) as expenses 'incurred in' the Vaccine Act proceeding. The court affirmed the special master's award on this ground.

4156: Denial of plaintiffs' motion for reconsideration under Rule 59 of the Court of Federal Claims, reviewed for abuse of discretion.
The court did not abuse its discretion by denying Plaintiffs' motion.
4171: Attorney fees under EAJA 28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)(2)(A): whether egregious agency procurement misconduct can be a 'special factor' justifying fees above the $125/hour cap; the Claims Court's enhanced fee award was vacated and remanded.

4280: Denial of Chrimar's motion for attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. 285; denial affirmed for abuse of discretion.
The district court did not abuse its discretion in making what here was a case-specific judgment
4342: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. 285: denial of fees affirmed, case not exceptional
we cannot say that it abused its discretion in denying fees.
4355: Denial of Merit Medical's motion under 35 U.S.C. § 285 for attorney fees as an exceptional case; affirmed.
We conclude that the district court did not abuse its discretion in denying Merit Medical's motion for attorney fees under § 285.
4368: Attorney fees and costs: the court granted Swedish Restaurant's motion for costs and attorney fees under FRAP 38 as the appeal was frivolous, and denied Bank's sanctions motion.

4428: Attorneys' fee award under 28 U.S.C. § 1498(a): the Claims Court's award of fees was upheld, including its finding that the government's litigation position was not substantially justified and its refusal to proportionally reduce fees for limited damages recovery.

4625: Casper's request for fees and costs for pre-settlement litigation under 35 U.S.C. §285, 28 U.S.C. §1927 and inherent power was denied (§285 request moot; other fees barred by settlement release), and the denial was affirmed.
We reject Casper's request for fees and costs relating to pre-settlement litigation under 28 U.S.C. § 1927 and the district court's inherent power.
4635: Prevailing-party determination under the settlement agreement's fee-shifting clause; ULC held to be the prevailing party entitled to attorney fees and costs
We hold that ULC is the prevailing party and is therefore entitled under the settlement agreement to recover reasonable attorney fees and costs incurred in connection with this action.
4663: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: the district court found the case exceptional and awarded Appellees $363,243.80 in fees and expenses, which the Federal Circuit affirmed as within its discretion.
Accordingly, the District Court did not abuse its discretion in concluding that Blackbird's case against Appellees is 'exceptional' within the meaning of 35 U.S.C. § 285.
4905: Exceptional-case fee award under 35 U.S.C. § 285 based on the patent infringement claim; reversed, so fees denied or vacated

we conclude that no adequate case has been made for finding that Munchkin's position and conduct relating to its patent infringement claim support a determination that this case is 'exceptional' under § 285.
4906: Exceptional-case fee award under 15 U.S.C. § 1117(a) based on the trademark infringement claims; reversed, so fees denied or vacated

the district court was required to make specific findings about the trademark infringement merits themselves, not merely presume the substantive weakness of the merits from Munchkin's choice to assert a slightly different trademark logo.
4907: Exceptional-case fee award under 15 U.S.C. § 1117(a) based on the trade dress infringement claims; reversed, so fees denied or vacated

4955: Motion for sanctions under FRAP 38 seeking attorneys' fees and double costs for a frivolous appeal, which the court denied.
It is due to the unique procedural posture here and the sequence of events in the evolution of this court's patent venue law that we deny 3M's motion for sanctions.
4995: Denial of attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285 for exceptional case; district court's exceptionality determination reviewed for abuse of discretion and affirmed.
Because we hold the district court did not abuse its discretion in denying Wright's motion for attorney fees under § 285, we affirm.
5050: Costs: LNC awarded chargeable costs as prevailing party under Fed. R. Civ. P. 54(d)(1) and 28 U.S.C. § 1920; award vacated.

5080: Whether 35 U.S.C. § 145's 'all the expenses of the proceedings' provision authorizes the PTO to recover its attorneys' fees from the applicant, given the American Rule; the court held it does not.

5216: Attorneys' fees and costs under the Vaccine Act: the Special Master's denial of fees and costs was vacated and remanded.
Because the Special Master abused his discretion in denying attorneys’ fees and costs, we vacate and remand.
5258: Prevailing party status under Rule 54(d) after a mootness dismissal following cancellation of the patent claims, and the resulting award of costs to Facebook; the court affirmed the costs award.
For the reasons above, we affirm the district court's award of costs to Facebook under Fed. R. Civ. P. 54(d).
5378: Vaccine Act attorneys' fees: denial of fees and costs for the appeal of the entitlement decision to the Federal Circuit, as lacking a reasonable basis, reviewed for abuse of discretion.

We agree with the Court of Federal Claims that the special master did not abuse his discretion in declining to award fees and costs associated with the Krakows' appeal of the entitlement decision to this court.
5402: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: the district court's denial of fees as not exceptional was an abuse of discretion; fee order vacated and remanded for consideration of ECT's manner of litigation and objective unreasonableness of claim 11.
By not addressing the "adequate evidence of an abusive pattern" of ECT's litigation, Newegg, 793 F.3d at 1352, the District Court failed to conduct an adequate inquiry and so abused its discretion
5436: Pre- and post-judgment interest calculation on supplemental damages using wrong judgment date
We agree with Hologic that the district court should have used June 3, 2019 as the relevant date for awarding pre- and post-judgment interest.
5452: Denial of attorney's fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285 because the accused infringer was not a prevailing party absent a final court decision with judicial imprimatur.
Because there is no final court decision here, Timney cannot be a prevailing party for purposes of attorney's fees under § 285.
6121: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: the award to the accused infringers was vacated because it depended on the erroneous dismissal and was otherwise flawed (presumption of validity and amendment timing).
We therefore vacate the district court's dismissal and vacate its subsequent award of attorney fees.
6162: Enhanced damages and attorney's fees award vacated because it rested on the willfulness finding

Because the jury's willfulness finding must be vacated, so too must the resulting enhanced damages and attorney's fees award by the district court, both of which were explicitly based on the willful infringement finding.
6260: Denial of additional discovery on the privity issue (procedural ruling on discovery; coded as trial case management)
we decline to hold that the Board abused its discretion when it concluded that additional discovery was not warranted in this case.
6282: Exceptional-case determination under 35 U.S.C. §285 affirmed: the district court did not abuse its discretion in finding the case exceptional, so fees may be awarded.
We affirm the district court's determination that this case is exceptional under § 285.
6283: Attorney fee award of about $51 million vacated because the district court did not establish a causal connection between the misconduct and the fees awarded; remanded for redetermination.
We therefore vacate the district court's fee award and remand for the district court to conduct the appropriate analysis in the first instance.
6318: Whether the district court abused its discretion in awarding 28 U.S.C. 1927 fees against counsel on the ground that counsel's patent-eligibility position under Alice lacked color
We agree with Gutride that neither the filing of this case nor Gutride's continuation of the litigation support a § 1927 award.
6319: Whether the district court abused its discretion in finding that counsel acted in bad faith in pursuing the litigation, including its venue opposition and failure to settle or issue a covenant not to sue, so as to support a 1927 fee award

6322: Attorney fees and costs: exceptional-case fee award under 35 U.S.C. § 285 and expert costs under inherent power affirmed
Accordingly, we affirm the district court's award of attorneys' fees under § 285.
6471: Attorney's fees under 35 U.S.C. 285 awarded to Eko based on ARM's unreasonable pursuit of noninfringement claims; Reyna would reverse the fee award.

6472: Attorney's fees under 35 U.S.C. 285 awarded to Eko for ARM's obviousness position; denial of summary judgment did not conclusively establish reasonableness.

6561: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: district court's award of fees to accused infringer as exceptional case affirmed
we hold that the court did not abuse its discretion in awarding SOTI its reasonable attorneys' fees.

Because the district court did not err in finding that Appellees are prevailing parties under 35 U.S.C. § 285 (2012), and did not abuse its discretion in awarding attorney fees and costs under that provision, we affirm.
6589: Attorney fee award under 28 U.S.C. 1498(a): Claims Court erred by relying on pre-litigation government conduct in the substantial-justification analysis (Hitkansut), so the fee award was vacated and remanded.

6590: Substantial justification of the government's reliance on expert Blount's feasibility analysis: Claims Court erred in finding it not substantially justified because the expert's skill was irrelevant; remanded for reconsideration.
The government argues, and we agree, that this was error.
6591: Substantial justification of the government's Figure 11 units position: court found no clear error in the Claims Court's finding that the government's position was not substantially justified.
We see no clear error in the Claims Court's factual findings here or its conclusion that the government's position here was not substantially justified.
6607: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: the district court's finding that the case was exceptional and its award of about $444,051 in fees were vacated because the court analyzed whether one discrete portion of the case was exceptional rather than whether the case overall was exceptional; remanded for analysis under the proper standard.
Because the district court did not find that the case overall was exceptional, we vacate its finding of exceptionality under § 285 and remand for an analysis under the proper legal standard.
6729: Whether a Rule 41(a)(1)(A)(ii) stipulated dismissal with prejudice is a Rule 54(a) judgment that supports a motion for attorney's fees; the district court's denial of fees was vacated and remanded.
We vacate the judgment of the District Court for the District of Oregon and remand for further proceedings consistent with this opinion.
6779: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: the district court denied DISH and SXM fee motions by holding they were not prevailing parties; the Federal Circuit held they are prevailing parties and vacated and remanded the denial.
we hold that DISH and SXM are prevailing parties. Accordingly, we vacate and remand the district court's order denying Appellants' motions for attorneys' fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285.
6780: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: district court denied fees to accused infringers as not an exceptional case; affirmed under abuse-of-discretion review.
Here, we cannot say that the district court abused its discretion in denying fees.
6791: EAJA attorney fees: whether Winters was a prevailing party under EAJA after the Veterans Court remanded the 2014 Board decision for judicial economy, so that fees were properly denied
We agree with the government that the Veterans Court correctly concluded that Winters is not a prevailing party under EAJA.
6815: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: denial of accused infringer's motion for exceptional-case fees, affirmed as no abuse of discretion.
6853: EAJA attorney fees: whether Robinson was a prevailing party entitled to fees for the Veterans Court remand, which the court denied
we affirm the Veterans Court's decision denying Robinson's application for attorney fees.
6908: Section 285 attorney fee award to UCP reversed because UCP is no longer a prevailing party after the non-infringement judgment was vacated/reversed in the Merits Appeal.
Because we vacated the district court's judgment in the Merits Appeal, we must reverse its decision to award attorney fees.
6909: UCP's cross-appeal for additional §285 fees and fees-on-fees denied; no basis remains for fees-on-fees once the fee award is reversed; cross-appeal dismissed.
Because we reverse the district court's decision regarding attorney fees, there is no longer a basis for awarding any fees-on-fees.
6910: Denial of expert fees under the court's inherent power, reviewed for abuse of discretion; no abuse found because the bad-faith bar was not met.
After reviewing the record facts, we cannot discern any abuse of discretion in the district court's determination that Balsam's conduct did not meet that bar.
6943: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: the district court's finding that the case was exceptional and its award of fees were upheld as no abuse of discretion.
Because the district court did not abuse its discretion in finding this case exceptional under § 285 and awarding attorney fees, we affirm the district court's order in its entirety.
6944: Amount of the § 285 fee award ($600,000), including the aggregate methodology and refusal to apportion fees issue-by-issue; the award was upheld.
On this record, we conclude that the district court's discretionary determination of fees is well-supported.
6953: Denial of attorneys' fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285 following inequitable conduct finding; vacated and remanded for explanation
We vacate the portion of the judgment denying attorneys' fees on the basis that this is not an exceptional case under § 285, and we remand to the district court for reconsideration.
7031: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: the district court's award of fees to Imperium as prevailing party was reversed because Imperium is no longer the prevailing party after the court reversed the infringement judgment.
Accordingly, Imperium is no longer the prevailing party, and we must reverse the award of attorney's fees at issue in this case.
7073: Denial of accused infringers' motion for attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285 (exceptional case determination), reviewed for abuse of discretion; court found no exceptional case, including that litigation costs exceeding potential damages is not a per se exceptional circumstance.
We hold the district court did not abuse its discretion in declining to find this an exceptional case under 35 U.S.C. § 285, we affirm.
7174: Exceptional-case determination under 35 U.S.C. § 285 and award of attorney fees to accused infringers based on inadequate pre-suit investigation of infringement and related pattern of misconduct

we see no abuse of discretion in the district court’s determination of exceptionality based on plaintiffs’ inadequate pre-suit investigation of infringement in these and related cases. We therefore affirm.
7187: Attorneys' fees under 285: fee award vacated and remanded because the court relied on the willfulness finding, and excessive hours must be removed.
Accordingly, we vacate the district court's award of attorneys' fees and remand for further consideration along with willfulness.
7401: Attorney fees under EAJA: whether the government's position was substantially justified, so fees were properly awarded
We hold that the Claims Court did not abuse its discretion in finding that the government's positions were not substantially justified.
7475: Attorney fees: award of fees for the two California actions under the court's inherent equitable powers (bad-faith forum shopping), affirmed
we hold that the district court did not abuse its discretion in awarding fees pursuant to its inherent equitable powers.
7476: Attorney fees: denial of fees for the related Delaware action and inter partes review proceedings, affirmed on the independent ground of discretion
we hold that the district court did not abuse its discretion in declining to award attorneys' fees for the related actions
7477: Prevailing-party status under 35 U.S.C. §285 based on two voluntary dismissals; majority did not decide it, so this is not coded as a holding; dissent in part would have found prevailing-party status

I dissent in part because I also believe that the district court did not err in determining that two voluntary dismissals without prejudice is sufficient to confer prevailing party status under 35 U.S.C. §285.
7517: EAJA attorney fee award: whether the Veterans Court properly reduced the fee award for initial record review because the claimant did not prevail on all claims; the Federal Circuit reversed the reduction and remanded to increase the award.
we reverse the decision of the Veterans Court with respect to its interpretation of § 2412 and its concomitant reduction in reimbursable attorney time spent on initial record review.
7538: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: the court affirmed the exceptional-case finding and the $5,187,203.99 fee award, including the Kessler-based objective baselessness finding and the attribution of $1,948,987.01 in fees to exceptional conduct. Judge Dyk dissented as to the portion of the award attributable to the Kessler argument, which he would remand.
We affirm the district court's finding that this case was exceptional under 35 U.S.C. § 285 and the total award of $5,187,203.99 in attorneys' fees.
7768: EAJA attorney fees: whether the government's overall position was substantially justified; the court reversed the Claims Court's fee award and remanded for dismissal of the EAJA motion.
Applying our standard of review, we hold that the Claims Court abused its discretion in making its judgment call, due to its errors in faulting justification for the government's overall position.
8032: Costs awarded to the opposer, Bertini, on appeal.
8096: Denial of attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285 for lack of evidence of pre-2015 fees and no exceptional conduct by Fleet.
We therefore conclude that the court did not abuse its discretion in determining not to award Surti attorney fees under § 285.
8198: Attorney fees: appeal of fee award dismissed for lack of appellate jurisdiction because award not yet quantified
Because the award has not been quantified, we lack jurisdiction.
8303: Attorney fees under the URA (42 U.S.C. § 4654(c)): denial of fees for co-plaintiff attorney-spouse Gordon Woodley's legal work, barred under Kay v. Ehrler as pro se representation; affirmed.
We therefore affirm the denial of fees.
8304: Reimbursement of reasonable litigation expenses (appraisal fee, Federal Circuit filing fee, URA legislative research fee) under the URA; denial vacated and remanded for reasonableness determination.
We hold that Denise Woodley may recover reasonable expenses even though she may not recover the attorney's fees she seeks for Gordon Woodley's work.
8371: Western Plastics' cross-appeal of the denial of attorneys' fees; no abuse of discretion, so the denial was affirmed.
Western Plastics has not demonstrated that the district court abused its discretion in declining to award fees since a finding of willfulness does not alone compel such a result
8424: Attorneys' fee award to Kaba left in place after denial of Rule 60(b) motion seeking relief from the fee award
For the foregoing reasons, we affirm the district court's order.
8457: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: the district court's award of fees to Amazon as an exceptional case, based on continued litigation of claims rendered baseless by claim construction and the weakness of the § 101 positions, was upheld.
We therefore affirm the district court’s decision to award attorney fees.
8589: Attorney fee award to Juggernaut under 35 U.S.C. § 285 vacated because Juggernaut is no longer a prevailing party.
We vacate the award of attorney's fees because Juggernaut is no longer a prevailing party, a status required to receive a fee award under 35 U.S.C. § 285.
8666: Default judgment: denial of application for an order of default because the government was not served and had timely moved to dismiss
Accordingly, we also affirm the Claims Court's denial of Mr. Bishay's request for an order of default.
8743: Attorney fees and costs: denial of Magnetize's fee motion under 35 U.S.C. § 285, 28 U.S.C. § 1927, RCW 19.108.040 and RCW 4.84.185, including the finding that discovery abuses were already addressed by sanctions and that the pre-suit investigation did not warrant fees.
We conclude that the district court did not abuse its discretion in denying Magnetize’s motion for attorneys’ fees under any of the statutes.
8896: Attorney fees under 5 U.S.C. § 7701(g)(1) in the interest of justice (Allen fifth factor): MSPB denial of fees affirmed as supported by substantial evidence.
we find no error in the MSPB's decision to deny an award of attorneys' fees and costs.
8980: Denial of attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285 (exceptional case) after the accused infringer prevailed on summary judgment of non-infringement; court held district court did not abuse its discretion in finding the case not exceptional under the totality of the circumstances.
We therefore affirm the district court's denial of attorney fees under § 285.
9060: EAJA attorney fees: the Veterans Court denied fees because the claimant was not a prevailing party after the VA granted TDIU and the petition was dismissed as moot; the Federal Circuit affirmed.
The Veterans Court properly denied Cavaciuti's application for attorney fees and expenses under the EAJA because he was not a prevailing party.
9126: Ethika's request for attorneys' fees and sanctions for a frivolous appeal under Fed. R. App. P. 38 was denied.
Thus, we decline to impose attorneys' fees or sanctions.
9400: Attorneys' fees as sanctions under the court's inherent power, awarded to SAP, JPMorgan and IBM for vexatious litigation conduct; the court affirmed the fee awards.
The District Court did not abuse its discretion in imposing monetary sanctions.
9464: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. §285 on Cisco's cross-appeal: fee award affirmed
We see no abuse of discretion by the district court in this regard and affirm its award of attorney fees.
9510: Award of costs to the appellant Conejo as the prevailing party on appeal.
9655: Award of graphics costs under §1920(4) reversed as outside the statute; printing costs affirmed
We agree that the district court abused its discretion in awarding Amazon $126,399.19 in graphics costs.
9712: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: district court's denial of FMC's motion for fees as not an exceptional case, affirmed for abuse of discretion
Because the district court did not abuse its discretion in denying FMC's § 285 motion, we affirm.
9818: Leave to amend the complaint was requested by the court and found not to cure the defects, so no amendment was permitted.
Appellants' supplemental briefing makes no demonstration that an amendment would resolve the problems with the original complaint.
9853: Denial of attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285 following dismissal of the '220 patent infringement suit.
We agree with ShieldMark that the district court did not abuse its discretion in denying attorney fees.
9939: Attorney's fees under EAJA (28 U.S.C. § 2412(b)): the district court's award to Hyatt as a prevailing party was vacated because Hyatt was no longer a prevailing party after the earlier remand in Hyatt I.
Because we previously vacated and remanded the district court's decision ordering the issuance of patents, Mr. Hyatt is no longer a prevailing party, and we vacate the award of attorney's fees.
9940: Expert witness fees under 35 U.S.C. § 145: the court affirmed the district court's denial of the PTO's request for expert witness fees because § 145's 'all the expenses of the proceedings' language does not overcome the American Rule.
But the phrase "[a]ll the expenses of the proceedings" in § 145 does not specifically and explicitly invoke expert witness fees. Accordingly, we affirm.
10034: Denial of Lacerta's 35 U.S.C. § 285 attorney fee motion (finding case not exceptional) was vacated because the prevailing-party threshold is no longer met.
we vacate it because a threshold requirement for fees under § 285 is no longer met now that we are vacating aspects of the district court's judgment
10051: Denial of Hilti's motion for attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285 (exceptional case).
The court did not abuse its discretion in concluding that "this case does not represent one of those rare cases that stands out from others due to its unreasonableness."
10091: EAJA attorney fees: Veterans Court denied pro se claimant's request for compensation for non-attorney legal research time under EAJA; Federal Circuit affirmed.
We have previously held pro se litigants are not entitled to attorney fees, including compensation for non-attorney time preparing for litigation, under EAJA.
10314: Affirmance of the district court's award of attorneys' fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285, and holding plaintiff's counsel personally liable for those fees
The district court did not abuse its discretion in awarding fees.
10315: Grant of appellate attorneys' fees and double costs under Fed. R. App. P. 38 because the appeal was frivolous as argued, with counsel jointly and severally liable
Having considered all the parties' filings, we hold Mr. Pirri's appeal has been frivolously argued. We, therefore, grant Defendants' request for fees and double costs.
10322: EAJA fee award under 28 U.S.C. § 2412(b): plaintiffs' common-fund theory does not impose additional fee liability on the Government, so the denial of fees is affirmed.
we agree that the common fund doctrine does not apply here in the manner proposed by Plaintiffs, and therefore we affirm the trial court's denial of fees under § 2412(b).
10323: EAJA fee award under 28 U.S.C. § 2412(d)(1)(A): trial court's determination that the Government's overall position was substantially justified is upheld under abuse-of-discretion review, so fees are denied.

we cannot say that it abused its discretion in concluding that these wins were sufficient to render the Government's overall position substantially justified such that fees under § 2412(d) are precluded.
10350: Denial of Pure Hemp's motion for attorney fees under § 285, § 1927 and inherent authority for failure to establish an exceptional case
For the foregoing reasons, we affirm.
10353: UCANN's request for sanctions for a frivolous appeal; the court held the appeal was not frivolous as filed or as argued
we deem this appeal not frivolous.
10491: Attorney fees under 42 U.S.C. § 300aa-15(e): the Special Master's denial of fees for lack of reasonable basis was vacated because she overlooked objective evidence (medical records, Dr. Kim's note, sworn affidavits) and improperly relied on counsel's conduct; remanded for discretionary fee decision.

For these reasons, we conclude that the Special Master clearly erred when conducting her reasonable basis analysis of Ms. James-Cornelius's claim. Because the decision to deny attorneys' fees rested solely on the absence of a reasonable basis, we vacate that decision and remand
10498: Attorney's fees under EAJA (28 U.S.C. § 2412(b)): the district court's award of fees to Hyatt was vacated because Hyatt is no longer a prevailing party after the earlier remand in Hyatt I.
Because we previously vacated and remanded the district court's decision ordering the issuance of patents, Mr. Hyatt is no longer a prevailing party, and we vacate the award of attorney's fees.
10499: Whether 35 U.S.C. § 145's phrase 'all the expenses of the proceedings' shifts the PTO's expert witness fees to the applicant; the court held it does not, so the denial of expert fees was affirmed.
we affirm the district court's denial of the PTO's request for expert witness fees.
10561: Attorney fees and costs awarded to Infinity as a discovery sanction for Sorrell's late production of the patent assignment, affirmed.
Thus, we affirm the district court's grant of attorney's fees and costs to Infinity.
10574: Award of attorney's fees and a $1,000 sanction against Leader following the contempt finding; the court reversed the award because the contempt finding lacked evidentiary support.
we reverse the district court's contempt order and its corresponding award of sanctions and attorney's fees.
10806: Attorney fees under EAJA: Court held Crawford was a prevailing party because the CFC remand was implicitly predicated on agency error and he succeeded on remand, reversing the denial of fees.
We hold the Court of Federal Claims erred in concluding Mr. Crawford was not a prevailing party under § 2412(d)(1)(A).
10807: Attorney fees under EAJA: Court held the government did not carry its burden to show its position was substantially justified.
The government has not carried its burden to show its position was substantially justified in this case.
10814: Monetary sanctions in the form of costs and attorney fees under Rule 37 for willful violation of the exclusion order.
We see no abuse of discretion in the court's decision to award sanctions in the form of costs and attorney fees under Rule 37 for willful violation of its prior order.
10903: Denial of Tolmar's motion for attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285 (exceptional case) affirmed; district court's totality-of-circumstances analysis and abuse-of-discretion review upheld.
the record reflects that the district court properly evaluated the totality of the circumstances consistent with the law.
10933: Attorney fee award from class common fund (5%, about $185 million) vacated and remanded for redetermination; Claims Court abused its discretion by dispensing with the lodestar cross-check promised in the class notices and by treating the fee request as presumptively correct.

Because the Claims Court's analysis was inconsistent with the terms of the class opt-in notices and did not adequately justify the extraordinarily high award, we vacate the award and remand for a redetermination of what fees should be awarded.
10935: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: district court's exceptional-case determination and award of fees on remand
the district court did not abuse its discretion in finding this case to be exceptional under § 285.
11079: Attorney fees and costs: whether the URA requires the government to reimburse fees retained by class counsel under contingent fee agreements beyond the reasonable lodestar fee awarded.

We do not read our prior statement to mean that the government must, on top of paying that reasonable fee, also reimburse Ms. Evans for further fees retained by counsel under a contingent fee agreement
11238: Attorneys' fees award under 35 U.S.C. § 285, vacated as a consequence of reversing the dismissal
Because we reverse the district court's dismissal of HCM's complaint, we also vacate the court's award of attorneys' fees.
11266: Attorney's fees: Board granted fees in part for the remand period and denied fees for representation before the Federal Circuit; affirmed.
We affirm the Board's decision granting in part Ms. Doyle's motion for attorney's fees.
11283: Request for refund of the filing fee and waiver of costs under USERRA 38 U.S.C. § 4323(h)(1); denied because no USERRA claim was filed.
As to his first request, USERRA waives any fees or courts costs for "any person claiming rights under this chapter." But Mr. Akerman has not filed a USERRA claim with the Board
11330: EAJA attorney's fees: the Board's award of fees under 5 U.S.C. 504 rested on a categorical narrowing of the substantial-justification inquiry, which the court held legally incorrect, so the fee decision was vacated and remanded for reconsideration.
We must vacate that decision and remand for reconsideration of the substantial-justification question without the categorical limitations reflected in the Fees Decision now before us.
11376: Attorney fees: whether employee is a prevailing party entitled to fees under the Back Pay Act and 5 U.S.C. § 7701(g) after the merits decision was mooted on review
We conclude that Ms. Neal may recover attorneys' fees as the prevailing party and reverse.
11618: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: district court held case exceptional and awarded fees to Vizio; affirmed
We affirm the district court's ruling granting an award of attorney fees to Vizio.
11731: Award of attorney's fees under the exceptional case standard, including the claim that the award was punitive; fee award affirmed.
Therefore, we affirm the award of attorney's fees to Dynamite.
11745: Attorney fees and costs under 35 U.S.C. § 285, 28 U.S.C. § 1927, and inherent power: the denial of fees and costs was vacated for lack of meaningful review, so fee denial is vacated in Pen-Tech's favor.
We vacate the court’s denial of Pen-Tech’s Rule 11 motion and motion for attorneys’ fees and costs under § 285, § 1927, and the court’s inherent power.
11784: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. 285: district court found the case exceptional based on objectively baseless infringement positions and awarded fees; affirmed.
We affirm the determination that this case is exceptional under 35 U.S.C. § 285.
11785: Non-taxable expenses, including expert fees, awarded under the district court's inherent power for bad faith or vexatious conduct; affirmed.

We cannot say the district court clearly erred in its assessment of the evidence as to these findings, and we therefore affirm the district court's decision to exercise its inherent power and award non-taxable expenses.
11786: Amount of fees and expenses, including whether the but-for causation standard of Goodyear permitted shifting all post-July 14, 2020 expenses; affirmed.

11787: Joint and several liability of Carnegie and M7D for the fee and expense award under Evident Corp.; affirmed.
we hold that it did not abuse its discretion in finding Carnegie and M7D jointly and severally liable.
11788: Denial of Fenix's request for prejudgment interest on the fee award as belated; affirmed.
we conclude that the district court did not abuse its discretion in finding Fenix's request to be belated under the circumstances of this case and thus denying it.
11810: EAJA attorney fee application: whether the veteran was a prevailing party entitled to fees after the Veterans Court vacated an ultra vires Board decision and dismissed the appeal

Where the Board acts ultra vires in preemptively issuing an adverse decision before any jurisdiction-conferring NOD is filed, the veteran's success in obtaining vacatur of that decision confers prevailing party status under EAJA.
11849: Attorney fees and costs: requests for EAJA fees and bid preparation costs were not considered because Monbo is not a prevailing party or likely to succeed
We thus do not consider these requests.
11967: Attorneys' fees: affirmed the award of fees for work on the contract claim under the confidentiality agreement's indemnity clause and California law.
We therefore affirm the district court's award of attorneys' fees.
12029: EAJA attorney fee application denied by the Veterans Court; the Federal Circuit vacated the denial because the court did not assess whether the VA's administrative position was substantially justified.
12157: Attorneys' fees under 35 U.S.C. 285 vacated because they relied in part on the negative inference from the contempt finding; remanded for reconsideration
The district court must reconsider the issue of fees unburdened by the negative inference from the contempt finding.
12320: EAJA attorney fees: whether VetLAG was a prevailing party entitled to fees after the mandamus petition was dismissed as moot following voluntary VA corrective action; the court affirmed denial of fees.

We therefore hold that a court order requiring a party only to confirm its voluntarily taken corrective actions for purposes of assessing mootness does not bear sufficient judicial imprimatur to confer prevailing-party status.
12445: Attorney fees under the Vaccine Act: the Special Master's denial of fees based on the Triple Risk Model (Boatmon) was an abuse of discretion because he did not analyze whether the theory was reasonable at filing; the fee denial was vacated and remanded.

Because the Special Master failed to analyze whether the Triple Risk Model was a reasonable causation theory at the time of filing, we conclude that he misapplied the law, which constitutes an abuse of discretion.
12678: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. section 285: the district court's no-exceptionality determination was vacated and remanded for explanation and an opportunity to argue, favoring the cross-appellant Farmers Edge.
Accordingly, we are constrained to vacate the district court's determination that the case is not exceptional and remand with instructions that the court reassess
12737: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. 285 awarded to Google as prevailing party in an exceptional case, based on inadequate pre-suit investigation and frivolous claims.

Based on these findings, it was not an abuse of discretion for the district court to determine this case is exceptional and to choose, therefore, to award attorneys' fees to Google as the prevailing party.
12740: Additional fees and costs awarded against EscapeX's attorneys, jointly and severally, under 28 U.S.C. 1927 for reckless filing of a frivolous Rule 59(e) motion.
Hence, the district court did not abuse its discretion in granting Google's § 1927 motion.
12881: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: denial of Incstores's motion for fees based on the absence of an exceptional case finding; affirmed.
12910: Request for attorney fees and costs for defending the appeal as frivolous as argued; court declined to award fees.
Although a close case on the frivolous as argued standard, we decline to impose attorney fees.
13082: Board denied employee's petition for attorney fees under 5 U.S.C. 7701(g)(1) because he was not a prevailing party after the agency unilaterally rescinded the appealed action; Federal Circuit affirmed.
Mr. Sanders has not shown, nor do we see, any error in the Board's reasoning or disposition.
13186: Section 285 exceptional-case finding and award of attorney fees to Castle after dismissal on §101 grounds; affirmed as no abuse of discretion.
we find that the district court did not abuse its discretion in determining—under the totality of the circumstances—that the case was exceptional under Section 285.
13218: Denial of attorney fees under 38 U.S.C. 5904(c)(1) for work performed before the initial AOJ decision notice; Board denial affirmed
Accordingly, the Veterans Court did not err in ruling that she was not entitled to attorney's fees under § 5904(c)(1).
13246: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: the district court's award of fees to defendants based on six red flags as an exceptional case was vacated for abuse of discretion and remanded.
We vacate and remand because the district court abused its discretion in determining the case exceptional for the reasons below.
13469: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: exceptional case finding and award of $207,543.60 affirmed
We agree with the district court that this was ample justification for awarding attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285.
13550: Attorney fees awarded to BPI as a sanction for the License Agreement misconduct, affirmed.
We affirm the Sanctions Order as to the attorneys’ fees.
13585: Exceptional-case finding under 35 U.S.C. § 285 and the award of about $6.9 million in fees reversed as moot, with the fee reasonableness also questioned on remand.
we reverse as moot the district court’s finding that AIT’s case was exceptional under § 285.
13633: Attorneys' fees awarded under 35 U.S.C. § 285 for an exceptional case; award upheld.
We hold that the district court acted within its discretion in awarding attorneys' fees and enhanced damages to SynQor.
13829: Denial of AeroVironment's motion for attorneys' fees under 35 U.S.C. 285; affirmed.
The district court's rejection of AeroVironment's characterization of the Arltons' case and their litigation conduct was not an abuse of discretion.
13835: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. §285 against mCom for an exceptional case; reversed because neither the invalidity, noninfringement, licensure, nor litigation-history grounds supported exceptionality.
In the circumstances here, we reverse the fees award under § 285.
13836: Sanction of $50,619.59 against counsel Brieant under 28 U.S.C. §1927 for unreasonably and vexatiously multiplying proceedings; reversed for lack of bad-faith or needless obstruction finding.
The district court found no other obstructive conduct related to this case, so we reverse the § 1927 sanction.
13865: Denial of the challenger's motion for attorney fees under §285 and costs; vacated because the challenger is the prevailing party and the exceptionality and costs determinations must be reconsidered on remand.

13908: Denial of leave to amend the complaint as futile because the claim was time-barred.
we cannot say the Claims Court abused its discretion because it is not unreasonable for the trial court to deny amendment where the statute of limitations on a claim bars relief.
14043: Attorney fees and costs under EAJA: the court affirmed the Veterans Court's limit on reimbursement of travel expenses, using prevailing market rates and excluding expenses not incurred solely for the litigation.
Accordingly, we affirm the Veterans Court's decision as to Mr. Delano's travel expenses.
14052: Denial of Alcor's motion for attorney's fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285 on the patent infringement claims
The district court did not abuse its discretion because it correctly found that Alifax's patent claims 'were not exceptional'
14053: Denial of Alcor's motion for attorney's fees under 17 U.S.C. § 505 on the copyright infringement claim
we hold that it was not an abuse of discretion for the district court to deny attorney's fees as to Alifax's copyright infringement claim.
14141: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: the district court found the case exceptional based on Viavi's pre-suit diligence, its reliance on a licensed filter, and its post-filing manner of litigation, and awarded fees accrued after the Wu Declaration. The Federal Circuit affirmed.

14181: Attorney's fees for work by Gordon Woodley during the Federal Circuit appeal and anticipated remand denied under the mandate rule and the prior ruling that pro se attorney-litigants cannot recover fees for their own interests
the mandate rule prohibits recovery of attorney's fees for work performed by Gordon Woodley during her appeal and on remand
14399: Denial of 35 U.S.C. § 285 attorney fees and costs incurred in the parallel IPR proceeding; under Dragon, IPR is a voluntarily undertaken parallel proceeding and not a case under § 285, so fees are not recoverable. Affirmed.
we hold that § 285 does not permit a party to collect attorney fees and costs from a voluntarily undertaken parallel IPR proceeding
14400: Exceptional-case determination under § 285 and award of attorney fees and costs to Nextremity for the district court litigation, including rejection of Extremity's burden-shifting and weighing arguments. Affirmed.
the district court did not abuse its discretion in finding the case to be exceptional under § 285 on the record before us
14448: Taxation of $589,343 in costs against plaintiffs, vacated and remanded because the prevailing-party and net-cost allocation must be reconsidered after the companion-case reversals.

14503: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285 - district court found case exceptional and awarded fees from January 3, 2022 onward; affirmed

14589: Inherent-power sanction award of $213,765 in fees and costs against plaintiffs for bad-faith conduct from December 2021 onward; affirmed.
We affirm the award under the district court's inherent power to sanction, which we review for an abuse of discretion.
14590: Inherent-power fee award of $4,750 for sealing-related costs under Local Patent Rule 2.2; vacated because the district court made no bad-faith findings and remanded.
we vacate the district court's award of $4,750 for fees and costs arising from the plaintiffs' violation of Local Patent Rule 2.2 and remand for the required findings.
14626: Section 285 exceptionality: district court found the cases exceptional and awarded fees to the accused infringers for time spent litigating, based on the substantive weakness of Dragon's infringement position; affirmed.
We hold the district court did not abuse its discretion in declaring these cases exceptional and affirm the district court's grant-in-part of Appellants' motions for attorneys' fees.
14627: Recoverability under §285 of fees incurred in the parallel, voluntarily pursued IPR proceedings; denied and affirmed.
We hold §285 does not entitle Appellants to recovery of fees incurred in parallel IPR proceedings and does not entitle Appellants to hold Dragon's counsel jointly and severally liable for fees.
14628: Whether §285 fees can be assessed jointly and severally against the patentee's former counsel (Freitas & Weinberg / Robert Freitas); denied and affirmed.
We agree with the district court's analysis and hold that liability for attorneys' fees awarded under § 285 does not extend to counsel.
14741: Section 285 fees: the district court denied fees because Realtek was not a prevailing party after Future Link's voluntary dismissal was converted to a dismissal with prejudice. The Federal Circuit held Realtek is a prevailing party and vacated the denial, remanding for an exceptional-case determination.

Under the circumstances of this case, Realtek is a prevailing party. We thus vacate the district court's § 285 decision and remand for the district court to consider whether this case is exceptional and whether fees are appropriate.
14742: Rule 54(d)(1) costs: the district court did not address Realtek's request for costs. The court held it abused its discretion by not addressing costs and remanded for an explanation.
Because the district court did not address costs under Rule 54 at all, we hold that it abused its discretion. We remand for the district court to address Rule 54 costs and explain its decision.
14743: Rule 11 sanctions and fees: the district court's denial of Rule 11 sanctions was affirmed because Future Link's pre-filing investigation was adequate and an improper purpose was not the but-for cause of the suit.
Accordingly, we affirm the district court's denial of Rule 11 sanctions in the 363 case.
14744: 28 U.S.C. § 1927 fees: the denial of fees under § 1927 in both cases was affirmed because Realtek did not show clear and convincing evidence that every facet of the litigation was patently meritless.
We thus affirm the district court's § 1927 decisions.
14940: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: HID was not a prevailing party because the Court of Federal Claims dismissed withdrawn claims without prejudice, so fees were denied.

We hold that, under our precedent, HID cannot be a “prevailing party” because the Court of Federal Claims permitted G&D to withdraw the claims then dismissed them without prejudice and, thus, G&D may refile or reassert the withdrawn claims against HID.
14987: Award of class counsel attorneys' fees of $23,863,345.02 under the percentage-of-the-fund method with a lodestar cross-check.
We find that the district court applied the correct legal standard and did not abuse its discretion.
15014: Whether claimant is a prevailing party under EAJA entitled to attorney fees; remand premised on administrative error, so prevailing party status found and fee denial reversed

Under these circumstances, the remand is most reasonably read as being implicitly based on administrative error, and thus we reverse the Veterans Court's determination that Mr. Louvall is not a prevailing party.
15061: Attorneys' fee award under exceptional-case finding vacated because fees must be apportioned between patent and trademark work.
Accordingly, we vacate the district court's attorneys' fees award.
15071: Attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285: the district court's exceptional-case finding and $9.1 million fee award were reversed because the court legally erred in treating Myriad as dispositive of the § 101 position, which was not exceptionally meritless.
In our view, it was legal error to treat Myriad as the beginning and the end of the patent-eligibility analysis for ChromaDex's claims.
15180: Denial of fees and expenses for class administrator under EAJA subsection (b): the court held EAJA subsection (b) provides no basis for shifting class administrator fees absent a statutory or common-law predicate or a settlement term.
EAJA subsection (b) therefore provides no basis for shifting those costs to the government.
15181: Fee award under EAJA subsection (d): the Claims Court's finding that the government's position was substantially justified is vacated and remanded for analysis of pre-litigation agency conduct; the litigation-position finding was affirmed.

we vacate and remand for the court to address the plaintiffs' claim that they are entitled to attorney fees and expenses based on their claim that the agencies' pre-litigation conduct was not substantially justified
15343: Rule 37(b)(2)(C) expense award against counsel (capped at 25,000 dollars) for violating the protective order
Nor did the district court abuse its discretion in setting the amount of sanctions.
15344: Denial of Lowe's motion for attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. 285 and sanctions under 28 U.S.C. 1927 on cross-appeal
We affirm the denial of the motion for fees and sanctions.
